ENGLISH: The Valley of Elah
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 以拉谷

ENGLISH: David & Goliath
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大卫与歌利亚

ENGLISH: A shepherd boy walks into a valley where an entire army has been silent for forty days.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一个牧童走进山谷，而整支军队已经在这里沉默了四十天。

ENGLISH: c. 1020 BC, in the Valley of Elah. The Israelite army and the Philistine army are camped on two ridges with a valley between them, and neither side has moved for forty days.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 约公元前 1020 年，以拉谷。以色列和非利士两支军队隔着山谷扎营，四十天来谁也没有动手。

ENGLISH: King Saul commands Israel. The Philistines have a champion named Goliath — close to three metres tall, in bronze scale armour, with a spear shaft like a weaver’s beam. Nobody in Israel will go out to him.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 以色列这边由扫罗王率领；非利士那边有一位名叫歌利亚的巨人，身高近三米，全身铜甲，枪杆粗得像织布的机轴，天天下来叫阵。以色列没有一个人敢出去。

ENGLISH: Both sides agreed to a deal: one fighter each, and the losing nation becomes servants. You are in the camp as a witness. You cannot change the ending — only what you do with the forty days.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 两边讲好了：各派一人单挑，输的那一国举国做奴仆。你是随军的一个见证者。结局你改不了，但在四十天里你要做什么、成为什么样的人，由你决定。

ENGLISH: David refuses Saul’s armour, takes five smooth stones from the brook, and faces Goliath with a sling. The point of the story is not that a small person can be brave — it is that the battle belongs to the LORD.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大卫脱下扫罗借给他的盔甲，从溪里捡了五块光滑的石子，用甩石的机弦迎上去。这个故事要说的不是「小人物也能赢」，而是这场仗本来就属于耶和华。

ENGLISH: You did not lift a stone. You learned where to look.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 石子不是你甩出去的。你真正学到的，是眼睛该往哪儿看。

ENGLISH: David’s courage came before his confidence: he remembered what God had already done with the lion and the bear. Faith grows by remembering.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大卫的勇气不是天生的。他先是想起神怎样救他脱离狮子和熊，然后才敢走向那个巨人。信心就是在回忆里一点点长出来的。

ENGLISH: Think of one “giant” in your life right now. What is the first step of faith for you?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你生命里现在有一个什么样的「巨人」？信心的第一步，对你来说会是什么？

ENGLISH: Remember what God has already brought me through
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 先回想神已经带我走过的路

ENGLISH: That is exactly where David started — not with the giant, but with the lion and the bear behind him. 1 Samuel 17:37
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大卫就是这样开始的——不是从巨人开始，而是从身后的狮子和熊开始。撒母耳记上 17:37

ENGLISH: Tell someone, so I am not facing it alone
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 找一个人说出口，不要一个人扛

ENGLISH: Wise. Even David asked questions of the whole line before he stepped forward. 1 Samuel 17:26
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这是智慧。大卫出阵以前，也先跟阵上的人说过话。撒母耳记上 17:26

ENGLISH: Refuse armour that does not fit me and simply start
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 脱掉别人给我的盔甲，用自己的方式上

ENGLISH: Saul’s armour was excellent — for Saul. Discernment is knowing which help is actually yours to carry. 1 Samuel 17:39
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 扫罗的盔甲很好——只是不合大卫。分辨力，就是分得清哪些帮助真的适合你。撒母耳记上 17:39

ENGLISH: The scroll grows warm in your hands. The ink shifts, campfires flicker into being, and the smell of dust and sheep fills the air.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 书卷在你手里发烫，墨迹像水一样流动。营火一盏一盏亮起来，尘土和羊群的气味扑到脸上。

ENGLISH: A man in a travel-stained scribe’s robe steps beside you. This is Corin, your companion on the road.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 有人在你身边站定，是个满身风尘、穿文士长袍的人。他叫柯林，此后一路与你同行。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: The Valley of Elah, around 1020 BC. Hear me clearly: we are witnesses. We cannot rewrite what God has written. But we can choose what kind of people we become while we watch.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「公元前一〇二〇年左右，以拉谷。」他低声说，「记住：我们只是见证人，改不了神写下的结局。能决定的，是我们自己成为怎样的人。」

SPEAKER: soldier
ENGLISH: Forty days. Forty mornings that giant has shouted at us, and not one man has answered.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 山谷对面，非利士人的军队已经骂阵四十天。四十天里，以色列没有一个人出去应战。

SPEAKER: goliath
ENGLISH: Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me! If he be able to fight with me and kill me, then will we be your servants — but if I prevail, then shall ye be our servants!
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你们拣选一个人，叫他下来到我这里来！他若能与我交战，把我杀了，我们就作你们的仆人。」

ENGLISH: The whole line of Israel shifts backward. Corin looks at you. So — where will you stand?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 喊声撞在两边山壁上。以色列全军往后退了一步。柯林看着你：你要站在哪里？

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Every choice here will leave a mark on you, not on the story. That is how the road works.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这里每一个选择，刻下来的都是你自己，不是故事。这条路的规矩就是这样。

ENGLISH: Walk to the front line and face the shouting
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 走到最前线去，迎着那声音

ENGLISH: Your legs do not feel brave, but they carry you forward. The giant’s voice fills your chest — and you stay.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你一点也不觉得自己勇敢，可你还是一步一步往前走。巨人的吼声压在胸口上——你没有退，就那样站着。

ENGLISH: Ask Corin what the Law says about fear
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问柯林，律法怎么说「不要怕」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Corin opens his scroll. “The officers shall say to the people: let not your hearts faint, fear not — for the LORD your God goeth with you.” You had heard it before. Today you need it.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 柯林展开书卷：「官长又要对百姓说：你们不要胆怯，不要惧怕他们，因为耶和华你们的神与你们同去。」

ENGLISH: Find the soldiers who are shaking and sit with them
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 到发抖的士兵中间坐下

ENGLISH: You sit in the dust beside a boy no older than sixteen. He stops trembling long enough to share his bread. Courage is easier when you are not alone.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你在一名不到十六岁的少年兵旁边坐下。他不再发抖，把自己仅有的饼掰了一半给你。

ENGLISH: A young man comes up the ridge from the baggage train, leading a donkey loaded with bread and cheese. He is small, sun-browned, and entirely unnoticed.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一个年轻人从辎重营那边爬上山脊，牵着一头驮着饼和奶酪的驴。他个子不高，晒得黝黑，没有谁多看他一眼。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: That is David, the youngest son of Jesse. He has been sent to bring food to his brothers. He was not invited to the battle.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 那是大卫，耶西最小的儿子。父亲派他来给几个哥哥送吃的——没有人叫他来打仗。

SPEAKER: goliath
ENGLISH: I defy the armies of Israel this day! Give me a man, that we may fight together!
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「我今日向以色列人的军队骂阵。你们叫一个人出来，与我交战吧！」

ENGLISH: David stops. His head tilts. He is listening — not to the size of the giant, but to what the giant is saying about God.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大卫停住脚步，侧过头去听。他听的不是那巨人有多壮，而是他在怎样谈论神。

ENGLISH: Tell David the king has offered a great reward
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 告诉大卫，王悬了重赏

SPEAKER: david
ENGLISH: David nods, but you can tell the reward is not what has caught him. He keeps looking at the giant.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大卫点点头，可你看得出来，让他动心的不是赏钱。他的眼睛始终没离开那巨人。

ENGLISH: Warn him that the whole army is afraid
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 提醒他全军都在害怕

SPEAKER: david
ENGLISH: You tell him plainly. David looks down the line of frightened men. “I see,” he says. He does not step back.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你照实说了。大卫望了望那排惊惶的人：「我看见了。」他没有往后退。

ENGLISH: Ask him about the lion and the bear
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问起狮子和熊的事

SPEAKER: david
ENGLISH: His whole face changes. “The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion and out of the paw of the bear — he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他整张脸都亮了：「耶和华救我脱离狮子和熊的爪，也必救我脱离这非利士人的手。」

ENGLISH: Word travels fast through a bored army. Within the hour David is standing in the tent of King Saul.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 营里的消息传得比人快。不到一个时辰，大卫已经站在扫罗的帐棚里。

SPEAKER: saul
ENGLISH: Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你不能去与那非利士人交战，因为你年纪太轻，他从小就作战士。」

SPEAKER: david
ENGLISH: Thy servant kept his father’s sheep, and there came a lion and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock. Thy servant slew both the lion and the bear. This uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, seeing he hath defied the armies of the living God.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你仆人为父亲放羊。有时来了狮子，有时来了熊，从羊群里叼走一只羊羔，你仆人就把狮子和熊都打死了。」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Saul has armour. It is the best in Israel. Watch what happens next.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 扫罗把自己的盔甲给大卫穿上——那是全以色列最好的一套。

ENGLISH: Offer David your own walking staff
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 把你的手杖递给大卫

SPEAKER: david
ENGLISH: He thanks you, smiling, and hands it gently back. “I have not proved these,” he says of the king’s armour. He takes his staff, his bag, and nothing else.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他笑着道谢，又轻轻还回你手里：「这些我从来没试过。」说完转身往溪边去了。

ENGLISH: Urge him to take the king’s sword anyway
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 劝他还是带上王的刀

SPEAKER: david
ENGLISH: He fastens it, takes two steps, and nearly falls. “I cannot go with these.” He unbuckles it. Corin raises an eyebrow at you.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他佩上刀，走了两步，差点绊倒：「穿这些我走不了路。」于是把刀解下来。柯林忍住笑，什么也没说。

ENGLISH: Say nothing. Watch what he does.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 什么也不说，看他怎么做

ENGLISH: A borrowed identity never fits in the valley. David walks out in a shepherd’s tunic.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 借来的身份，穿在身上总不合身。大卫穿着牧人的外衣走了出去。

ENGLISH: The brook runs shallow and cold through the valley floor. David kneels and turns over stones until he finds five that sit perfectly in his palm.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 溪水又浅又凉，从谷底穿过。大卫跪下去，在石缝里翻找，直到摸到五块正好握在手心的石子。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Five smooth stones. People love to guess what the five mean — the five books of the Law, five wounds, five something. The text simply says five smooth stones. Sometimes the honest reading is the better one.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 五块光滑的石子。有人爱猜「五」是什么意思——五卷律法、五处伤口。经文只说：五块光滑的石子。

SPEAKER: david
ENGLISH: He is a man, and I am a man. But he comes with a sword and a spear and a shield — and I come in the name of the LORD of hosts.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「他是人，我也是人；他靠的是刀、枪、盾牌，我靠的是万军之耶和华的名。」

ENGLISH: David looks at you. “Will you stand with me until the line?”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大卫回头看你：「你愿意陪我走到阵前吗？」

ENGLISH: Kneel and pray with him before he runs
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 跪下和他一起祷告

ENGLISH: The two of you bow beside the water. No thunder, no sign — just a quiet certainty that you are not the centre of this story.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你们一起在水边伏下身。没有雷声，也没有异象，你心里却安静地知道一件事：你不是这个故事的中心。

ENGLISH: Pick up a stone of your own and hold it tight
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 自己也捡一块石头，握紧

ENGLISH: The stone is ordinary. That is the strange part. God has always liked using ordinary things.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 那块石子普通得有点可笑。可妙就妙在这里——神一向喜欢用普通的东西。

ENGLISH: Step back and let him go alone
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 退一步，让他自己去

ENGLISH: You watch him walk down into the valley. Some roads can only be walked by one person at a time.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你看着他走下山谷。有些路，只能一个人走。

SPEAKER: goliath
ENGLISH: Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air and to the beasts of the field!
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「我岂是狗呢，你竟拿杖来攻击我？来吧，我要把你的肉给空中的飞鸟、田野的走兽吃！」

SPEAKER: david
ENGLISH: Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你来攻击我，是靠刀枪和盾牌；我来攻击你，是靠万军之耶和华的名。」

ENGLISH: David runs toward the line. He reaches into his bag. The whole valley seems to hold its breath — and Corin grips your sleeve.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大卫朝阵前跑去，手伸进袋子。整座山谷好像一下子屏住了呼吸——柯林抓紧你的袖子。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Do not look away. Whatever you do, do not look away.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「别移开眼睛。不管发生什么，都别移开。」

ENGLISH: The stone sinks into the giant’s forehead. Goliath falls face down into the dust of the valley he had mocked for forty days.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 石子陷进巨人的额头。歌利亚脸朝下，扑倒在他骂了四十天的那片尘土里。

ENGLISH: The Philistine line breaks. The army of Israel finds its voice all at once.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 非利士人的阵线一下子散了，以色列全军在同一刻找回了声音。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: And there it is. Not a story about a boy beating a giant. A story about a God who keeps His promises — and a boy who knew Whose battle it was.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这从来不是「小男孩打败大巨人」的故事，而是一位守约的神，和一个知道这场仗不属于自己的少年。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Come. The road goes on, and the scroll is already turning.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 书卷自己翻过一页。前面的路还在。

ENGLISH: The Lions’ Den
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 狮子坑

ENGLISH: Daniel in Babylon
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 巴比伦的但以理

ENGLISH: A decree is signed that makes prayer illegal. An old man opens his window anyway.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一纸法令把祷告定成死罪。一位年近八十的老人，照旧把窗开向耶路撒冷。

ENGLISH: c. 539 BC, in Babylon. The empire has just changed hands, and the new ruler, Darius the Mede, is reorganising the government.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 约公元前 539 年，巴比伦。帝国刚刚易主，新王大利乌正在重整朝政。

ENGLISH: Daniel was carried off from Jerusalem as a teenager. He is nearly eighty now, and the king has just put him in charge of the whole province. The other officials hate him for it.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 但以理少年时被掳离开耶路撒冷，如今已年近八十。王刚任命他总管全国，其他的官员因此恨他。

ENGLISH: They can find no corruption in him, so they attack his prayer. A law is drafted: for thirty days nobody may pray to anyone except the king. Break it and you go into a pit of lions — and a Persian law cannot be revoked, not even by the king who signed it.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他们查不出他贪污受贿，就把矛头对准他的祷告：三十天内，除了王，谁也不许向神或向人求什么。违者扔进狮子坑。波斯的律法一旦颁布就不能收回，连王自己也不行。

ENGLISH: Daniel is roughly eighty years old here. The decree was engineered by jealous officials who knew the one thing Daniel would not compromise: prayer, three times a day, facing Jerusalem.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这时但以理已经年近八十。这道禁令是嫉妒他的官员设的局——他们知道但以理唯一不肯让步的，就是一天三次、面向耶路撒冷的祷告。

ENGLISH: Integrity is what you do when the law changes and God has not.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 正直不是出了事才拿出来的东西，而是出事以前就一点点养成的习惯。

ENGLISH: Daniel did not become faithful in the lions’ den. He became faithful over decades of ordinary prayer — so that when the crisis came, there was nothing to decide.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 但以理不是在狮子坑里才变得忠心的。他是在几十年平淡的祷告里，一天一天变得忠心——所以真的起风浪时，他根本不用临场做决定。

ENGLISH: When doing the right thing costs you, what actually helps you keep going?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 当做对的事要付出代价，真正撑住你的是什么？

ENGLISH: A habit I already have, so I do not have to decide in the moment
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一个早就养成的习惯，让我不用临时硬撑

ENGLISH: That is Daniel’s gift to us. Three times a day, long before the decree. Daniel 6:10
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这正是但以理留给我们的。禁令还没来，他已经一天祷告三次。但以理书 6:10

ENGLISH: People who will wait with me through the night
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 愿意陪我熬过这一夜的人

ENGLISH: The story quietly mentions the king fasting all night. Even desperate company matters. Daniel 6:18
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 经文里提到，王那一夜禁食、睡不着。连帮不上忙的陪伴也算数。但以理书 6:18

ENGLISH: Remembering God can deliver me, whether or not He does
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 相信神能救我——也接受祂不一定照我的方式救

ENGLISH: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego said the same thing a generation earlier. Daniel 3:17–18
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 上一代的三个年轻人也说过同样的话。但以理书 3:17–18

ENGLISH: The scroll turns. Cedar, hot brick, and the noise of a vast city. You are standing in the shadow of a palace in Babylon.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 书卷翻动。香柏木、烤热的砖、一座大城的喧闹。你站在巴比伦王宫的影子里。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Daniel is an old man now — near eighty. He has outlived kings and empires. King Darius is about to set him over the whole realm.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 但以理已经老了，将近八十。他熬过了几个王朝，比许多君王都活得久。大利乌王刚刚提他总管全国。

SPEAKER: satrap
ENGLISH: We shall not find any occasion against this Daniel, except we find it against him concerning the law of his God.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「我们要找这但以理的把柄，除非在他神的律法里找。」说话的是几个同僚，声音压得很低。

ENGLISH: The officials drift toward the throne room with a parchment in their hands. Corin’s jaw tightens.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他们捧着一份写好的文书，往王座大殿走去。柯林的下巴绷紧了。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: They are going to make faithfulness illegal. What do you do with what you just heard?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他们要做的，是把忠心变成犯法。你听见了——现在你要怎么做？

ENGLISH: Read the decree as it is posted in the gate
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 到城门口去，把那道禁令读一遍

ENGLISH: You memorise the wording: thirty days, no petition to any god or man except the king. The penalty is the lions’ den. The trap is aimed at one man.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你把条文记在心里：三十天之内，除了王，不许向任何神或人求什么；违者扔进狮子坑。这道法令，从头到尾只为了一个人。

ENGLISH: Warn Daniel that the officials are watching him
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 去提醒但以理：有人正盯着他

SPEAKER: daniel
ENGLISH: He thanks you with real warmth. Then he asks whether you would like to pray — it is nearly the ninth hour.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他很诚恳地向你道谢，然后问你愿不愿意一起祷告——快到申初了。

ENGLISH: Ask Corin why they hate a man who has done no wrong
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问柯林，他们为什么恨一个没做错事的人

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: “Because a blameless life is a mirror,” Corin says. “And some people cannot bear what they see in it.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「因为无可指摘的人像一面镜子，」柯林说，「有些人受不了自己在镜子里看见的东西。」

ENGLISH: The ink is barely dry. The law of the Medes and Persians cannot be altered — not even by the king who signed it.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 墨迹还没干。玛代和波斯的律例一旦颁布就不可更改——连签字的王也不能改。

SPEAKER: darius
ENGLISH: It is signed. Let it be done.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「已经盖印了，就这样办吧。」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Daniel knows. He heard the herald in the street. Watch what he does with that knowledge.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 但以理知道这事。他在街上听过传令官的宣告。看看他拿这个消息做什么。

ENGLISH: An official passes close to you, smiling. “Thirty days,” he says. “Surely any reasonable man can wait thirty days.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一名官员笑着从你身边走过：「不过三十天。懂道理的人都等得起。」

ENGLISH: Tell Daniel to pray privately — just for thirty days
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 劝但以理先躲起来祷告，就这三十天

SPEAKER: daniel
ENGLISH: Daniel listens, then shakes his head, not unkindly. “If I hide it now, I have already agreed that the decree is true.” He reaches for the window latch.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 但以理听完，温和地摇摇头：「我要是现在躲起来，就等于承认那道禁令是对的。」说完，他伸手去推开窗。

ENGLISH: Ask whether the king can be persuaded to change the law
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 去问王能不能收回这道法令

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Corin sighs. “Not this law. That is the snare. The officials made mercy impossible, and they know the king loves him.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 柯林叹了口气：「这条路走不通。这就是圈套——他们让王没有退路，而他们知道王喜欢但以理。」

ENGLISH: Say nothing. Follow him at the ninth hour.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 什么也不说，到申初跟着他上楼

ENGLISH: You follow him to the upper room, and you are not the only one watching. Two officials are already in the courtyard below.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你跟着他上楼。你不是唯一在看着的人：院子里已经站着两名官员。

ENGLISH: The upper room is plain. A mat, a scroll, a window open toward Jerusalem — hundreds of miles away, and yet the direction matters.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 楼上很简朴：一张席子、一卷书、一扇朝耶路撒冷开的窗。隔着几百里路，方向仍然要紧。

ENGLISH: Daniel kneels. His knees are not what they were. He gives thanks, exactly as he had done before.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 但以理跪下去。膝盖早就吃不消了，他还是照样献上感谢。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Three times a day. Not as protest. Not as performance. Habit formed over a lifetime is what holds a person up when the law changes overnight.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一天三次。这不是抗议，也不是表演，而是一辈子养成的习惯——所以法律一夜之间变了，他也没有跟着塌下来。

SPEAKER: daniel
ENGLISH: You may stand at the window if you are afraid of being seen. I will not be.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你要是怕被人看见，可以站在窗边望风。我不怕。」

ENGLISH: Kneel beside him and pray
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 跪在他旁边，一起祷告

ENGLISH: The two of you pray while sandals scramble in the courtyard below. The prayer is short. It is enough.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你们祷告的时候，院子里响起急促的脚步声。祷告很短，但已经够了。

ENGLISH: Stand at the window as a lookout
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 站到窗边替他望风

ENGLISH: You see the officials exchange a look and hurry off toward the throne room. There is no time left to hide.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你看见那几名官员交换了一个眼神，匆匆往王宫去。已经来不及躲了。

ENGLISH: Ask him how he can give thanks right now
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问他：这种时候怎么还谢得出来

SPEAKER: daniel
ENGLISH: “Because thanksgiving is not a report on my circumstances,” he says. “It is a report on my God.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「因为感谢不是汇报我的处境，」他说，「是汇报我的神。」

SPEAKER: satrap
ENGLISH: That Daniel, which is of the children of the captivity of Judah, regardeth not thee, O king, nor the decree that thou hast signed, but maketh his petition three times a day.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「那被掳来的犹大人但以理，不理你，也不遵守你盖了印的禁令，竟然一天三次祷告。」

ENGLISH: Darius is furious — at himself. He works until sunset to find a way to undo his own law, and finds none.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大利乌王气极了——其实是气自己。他一心想救但以理，一直想到日落，还是想不出办法。

SPEAKER: darius
ENGLISH: Thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你所常事奉的神，祂必救你。」

ENGLISH: A stone is rolled over the mouth of the den. The king seals it with his own signet, and the nobles seal it with theirs.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一块石头滚过来，封住坑口。王用自己的印封了，贵族们又用他们的印封了。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: He is gone. And we are still here. That is often the hardest part of the story — being the ones left outside the stone.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 坑里已经没有声音了，我们还在外面。有时候最难的，不是替他进去，而是只能待在外面等。

ENGLISH: Go to the king and beg him to break his own law
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 去求王破例改自己的律法

SPEAKER: darius
ENGLISH: The king receives you with a tired face. He has already tried everything. He asks you to stay, and to wait until morning.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 王疲惫地见了你。能试的办法他都试过了。他请你留下来，等到天亮。

ENGLISH: Stay at the mouth of the den all night
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 在坑口守一整夜

ENGLISH: You sit with your back against the sealed stone. Cold seeps through your cloak. You do not sleep. Neither does the king, you will learn.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你背靠着那块封住的石头坐下。寒气透过斗篷渗进来。你没有睡——后来你才知道，王也没有睡。

ENGLISH: Gather the household servants to pray until dawn
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 把家里的人叫来，一起祷告到天亮

ENGLISH: Twelve of you sit in a circle on the floor. Someone begins a psalm; others join. The night does not get shorter, but it gets lighter.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 十几个人在地板上围坐成一圈。有人起了一首诗的调子，别人跟着唱。那一夜并没有变短，只是没那么难熬了。

ENGLISH: First light. The king comes in haste to the den, and his voice cracks before he reaches the stone.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 天刚亮，王就赶到坑边。人还没走到石头前，声音已经哑了。

SPEAKER: darius
ENGLISH: O Daniel, servant of the living God, is thy God, whom thou servest continually, able to deliver thee from the lions?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「永生神的仆人但以理啊，你所常事奉的神能救你脱离狮子吗？」

ENGLISH: A pause. Then, from inside the earth, a voice — calm, amused almost, entirely alive.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一阵沉默。然后地底下传来一个声音——平稳，甚至带点笑意，活得好好的。

ENGLISH: Hold your breath and listen
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 屏住呼吸，侧耳去听

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Sometimes the faithful thing is simply to stop talking and hear what God has done.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 有时候，最要紧的忠心就是先闭上嘴，听听神已经做成了什么。

ENGLISH: Fall to your knees on the cold stone
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 跪在冰冷的石头上

ENGLISH: You are not the only one. Half the courtyard is on its knees before Daniel finishes speaking.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 跪下的不止你一个。但以理还没答完，半个院子的人都已经伏在地上。

ENGLISH: Look for the angel Corin told you about
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 去找柯林说的那位使者

ENGLISH: You see nothing but a shaft of gold light from the grate above. That is more than enough.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你什么也没看见，只有一道光从上面的栅栏漏下来。那已经够了。

SPEAKER: daniel
ENGLISH: O king, live for ever. My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「愿王万岁！我的神差遣使者，封住狮子的口，叫狮子不伤我，因我在神面前无辜。」

ENGLISH: Daniel is lifted out. No wound on him — because he had believed in his God.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 但以理被拉上来，身上没有一点伤——因为他信靠他的神。

ENGLISH: The king writes to every nation under heaven: “He is the living God, and stedfast for ever, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 王又向天下各国颁布谕旨：「祂是永生神，永远长存；祂的国永不败坏。」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: He was not delivered from the decree. He was delivered through it. There is a difference, and you will need to know it.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 神没有让但以理绕过这道法令，而是让他走过了这道法令。这两件事不一样，差别值得你慢慢想。

ENGLISH: The Road to Jericho
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 耶利哥路上

ENGLISH: The Good Samaritan
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 好撒玛利亚人

ENGLISH: A lawyer asks Jesus a question. Jesus answers with a story — and you wake up inside it.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一个人被强盗打个半死，躺在路边。三个人走过，只有一个停下来。

ENGLISH: c. AD 30, on the road from Jerusalem down to Jericho — seventeen miles of limestone cliffs, sharp bends, and no soldiers.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 约公元 30 年，从耶路撒冷下耶利哥的那条路——十七英里的石灰岩山道，弯多，没有兵丁巡守。

ENGLISH: A lawyer has just tested a teacher named Jesus with a question: “Who is my neighbour?” Jesus answers with a story, and you find yourself standing inside it.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一位律法师刚刚用问题试探耶稣：「谁是我的邻舍？」耶稣没有正面回答，而是讲了一个故事，而你此刻就站在故事里面。

ENGLISH: A traveller lies beaten in the ditch. A priest and a temple assistant have already seen him and crossed the road. Someone still has to stop — and in this story the one who stops is the man nobody expects.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一个旅人被打个半死，躺在沟边。祭司和圣殿的助手已经先后从另一边走了过去。总得有人停下来——而在这个故事里，停下来的正是最出人意料的那个人。

ENGLISH: A lawyer asks “who is my neighbour?” wanting to limit the obligation. Jesus tells a parable in which the religious professionals pass by and a despised Samaritan stops — then turns the question around: which of the three was a neighbour?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 律法师问「谁是我的邻舍」，其实是想给责任划一条边界。耶稣没跟他辩，只讲了一个故事：该懂的人绕道走了，被看不起的撒玛利亚人却停下——然后反问：这三个人里，谁是那落在强盗手中之人的邻舍？

ENGLISH: Mercy is a verb with a price tag.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 怜悯不只是一个感觉而已，是要付上代价的。

ENGLISH: The Samaritan’s compassion cost him oil, wine, money, time, reputation, and his own donkey. Love that costs nothing is usually just a feeling.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 撒玛利亚人为这份怜悯付上了代价：油、酒、银子、时间、名声，还有他自己那头驴。不肯付代价的爱，多半只是一时心软。

ENGLISH: Who is the neighbour you find it hardest to love — and what would one small act look like?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 谁是你现在最难去爱的邻舍？一个很小的动作，可以是什么？

ENGLISH: Someone whose views I cannot stand
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一个我完全没法认同的人

ENGLISH: The Samaritan and the Jew disagreed about almost everything sacred. The bandage came first. Luke 10:33–34
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 撒玛利亚人和犹太人在几乎每件神圣的事上都不对付。可他还是先缠上了绷带。路加福音 10:33–34

ENGLISH: Someone I can help, but it will genuinely cost me
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一个我帮得了、但真的要付出代价的人

ENGLISH: Two denarii was real money. Count the cost honestly — then give anyway. Luke 10:35
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 二两银子是实打实的工钱，差不多是两天的收入。先老实算算要付多少，然后还是照样给出去。路加福音 10:35

ENGLISH: Someone I have walked past without really seeing
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一个我天天经过、却从没真正看见的人

ENGLISH: The priest “saw him” and passed by. Seeing is not the same as noticing. Luke 10:31
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 祭司「看见他」，就从那边过去了。看见了，不等于放在心上。路加福音 10:31

ENGLISH: You are sitting in the dust outside a village, listening to a teacher. A lawyer stands to test Him.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你坐在村外的尘土里，听一位老师讲道。一名律法师站起来试探他。

SPEAKER: lawyer
ENGLISH: Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life? … And who is my neighbour?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「夫子，我该做什么才可以承受永生？……谁是我的邻舍呢？」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: He is not asking for information. He is asking where the boundary is — who he is allowed to leave out.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他不是来求答案的。他想问的是：这条线划在哪儿，谁可以被划在外面。

SPEAKER: jesus
ENGLISH: A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves…
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「有一个人从耶路撒冷下耶利哥去，落在强盗手中……」

ENGLISH: The road rises up around you: seventeen miles of switchbacks, limestone, and shadowed places perfect for an ambush. You are in the story now.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 四周的路忽然立了起来：十七英里的急弯、石灰岩、正适合埋伏的阴影。你已经站在故事里了。

ENGLISH: Walk fast, before the sun gets high
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 趁着日头还低，快点走

ENGLISH: You make good time. That is the trouble with hurrying — you arrive at the bad part sooner.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你走得很快。麻烦也在这儿——你更早到了那段险路。

ENGLISH: Walk with a companion and keep your eyes open
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 结伴走，留意四周

ENGLISH: You notice the fresh blood before you notice the man. Your companion grips your arm.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你先看见新鲜的血迹，才看见那个人。同伴抓紧了你的手臂。

ENGLISH: Pray for safety on the road before you set out
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 出发前先为路上的平安祷告

ENGLISH: You ask God to make you useful, not just safe. It is a dangerous prayer, though you do not know it yet.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你求神让你成为一个有用的人，而不只是个安全的人。这祷告很危险，当时你还不知道。

ENGLISH: Halfway down, in a bend of the road where the rock walls close in, a man is lying in the dust.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 走到半路，一处岩壁收紧的弯道里，有人躺在尘土中。

ENGLISH: The thieves have stripped him, beaten him, and left him half dead. His breathing is shallow. There is no one else in sight.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 强盗剥去了他的衣裳，把他打个半死。他的呼吸很浅，四下里没有别人。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: This is where the parable gets uncomfortable. Everyone who comes down this road has to decide something.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 故事讲到这里，就不那么好听了。每一个从这条路走过的人，都得做个决定。

ENGLISH: Cross to the far side — it could be a trap
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 绕到另一边去——说不定是圈套

ENGLISH: You give him a wide berth. Your heart is still hammering when you reach the next bend. Being safe and being right are not the same thing.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你绕得很远。走到下一个弯时，心还在乱跳。安全是一回事，做对是另一回事，这两件事并不总在一起。

ENGLISH: Kneel and check if he is still breathing
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 跪下探一探他还有没有气

ENGLISH: He is alive. Barely. You tear a strip from your own cloak and press it against the worst wound. There is not much else you can do.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他还活着，勉强活着。你从自己的斗篷上撕下一条布，按住最深的伤口。你能做的也只有这些。

ENGLISH: Shout for help from the ridge above
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 朝山脊上喊人

ENGLISH: Your voice echoes off the limestone. Nobody answers — but two figures appear at the top of the road.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 喊声在石灰岩之间撞来撞去。没有人回应——但那人的手指动了一下。他听见了。

ENGLISH: You are kneeling in the dust with blood on your hands when you hear sandals on the stone.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你在他身边蹲下来。他需要的不只是同情，还要油、酒、绷带，和一头能驮他的牲口。

ENGLISH: A priest comes down the road. He sees the man — clearly sees him — and passes by on the other side.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 远处有脚步声。一个祭司从坡上下来，正往圣殿的方向去。

ENGLISH: Later, a Levite does exactly the same.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他看见了他。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Do not be too quick to despise them. They may have been afraid, or late, or certain that touching a corpse would make them unclean. Good reasons are always available.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 然后他从另一边走了过去。接着是一名利未人，也一样绕开了。

ENGLISH: Shout after them to come back
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 追上去问那两个人为什么

ENGLISH: They do not turn around. Your voice cracks on the last word. The man at your feet does not notice.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他们都有理由：礼仪上的洁净、律法的规定、怕惹麻烦。理由从来不缺。而那个人还躺在尘土里。

ENGLISH: Stay with the wounded man and keep pressure on the wound
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 留下来，尽力先把伤口包好

ENGLISH: You stay. It is unglamorous and it takes a long time. Most mercy looks exactly like this.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你的手在抖，还是把布条系紧了。柯林在旁边轻声说：「记住这一刻，你正在做一件神圣的事。」

ENGLISH: Ask Corin why the holy men walked away
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 走到路中间，拦下下一个路人

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: “Because knowing the Law and loving your neighbour are not the same achievement,” he says quietly. “I have been both men.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你拦下一个过路的人。他看看地上的人，又看看自己的行程，摇摇头走了。

ENGLISH: On the road, a priest comes down, sees the body, and crosses to the far side. A Levite follows, does the same, and is gone.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 第三个人骑着驴过来。他不是祭司，也不是利未人，是撒玛利亚人——本地的犹太人宁可绕路也不跟他说话的那种人。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: They had Scripture memorised. They were on their way to the temple. And the man in the ditch was still in the ditch.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他看见那人，就动了慈心。

ENGLISH: Then a third traveller appears, leading a donkey — and from his dress, he is a Samaritan. The wounded man is a Jew. The two peoples have hated each other for centuries.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他下驴，把油和酒倒在他的伤处，包扎好，扶他骑上自己的牲口，送到客店里去。

ENGLISH: He stops. He kneels. He pours oil and wine on the wounds.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 路上的每一个决定，其实都只用了短短几秒。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Watch closely. This is the part of the story people remember.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 柯林轻声提醒：注意，耶稣没说这个人是「好人」，只说他「动了慈心」。

ENGLISH: Go down and offer to carry his supplies
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 帮他一起把伤者抬上驴背

SPEAKER: samaritan
ENGLISH: He looks up, surprised, then nods as if this is the most natural thing in the world. “Hold the oil,” he says. “I will lift him.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你们一起把人抬上去。他沉，路远。撒玛利亚人一路牵着驴走。

ENGLISH: Ask him why he is helping an enemy
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问他为什么肯为一个陌生人停下

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: He does not answer. He simply keeps bandaging. Corin says: “The parable never tells us his reasons. I think that is deliberate — mercy that needs a reason can be argued away.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他想了一会儿：「因为要是躺在那儿的是我，我也盼着有人肯停一下。」

ENGLISH: Take the donkey’s lead rope and follow
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 先跑去客店把房间打点好

ENGLISH: The donkey is calm. The man on its back is not. You lead them both down the long road toward an inn.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你先跑到客店。店主起初不太情愿——直到看见那枚银币。

ENGLISH: The Samaritan finishes the bandage and lifts the man onto his own donkey, standing him up carefully as if he were something fragile.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你要尽心、尽性、尽力、尽意爱主你的神；又要爱邻舍如同自己。」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: He has somewhere to be too. His journey is now slower, his beast is carrying a stranger, and his oil is nearly gone. Compassion always spends something.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 律法师想证明自己问得有理，又追问：「谁是我的邻舍呢？」

SPEAKER: samaritan
ENGLISH: Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 耶稣把问题翻了个面：这三个人里，哪一个才是那落在强盗手中之人的邻舍？

ENGLISH: At the inn the Samaritan sets two denarii on the counter — about two days’ wages — and makes the innkeeper promise to look after the man.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 客店里，撒玛利亚人拿出二两银子——差不多是两天的工钱。

SPEAKER: innkeeper
ENGLISH: Two days’ wages? For a stranger?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你且照应他，此外所费用的，我回来必还你。」

SPEAKER: samaritan
ENGLISH: When I come again, I will repay thee whatsoever thou spendest more.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这不是一时的感动，而是一份要继续下去的承诺。他还会回来。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: He does not just feel pity. He commits money, time, and his own return journey. That is what makes it love instead of a sentiment.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 柯林说：怜悯很少是一时的心情，多半是一个决定，还要算上一笔代价。

ENGLISH: Offer to sit with the man through the night
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 替他把欠店主的账一笔笔记清楚

ENGLISH: You take the stool by the bed. Somewhere around midnight he opens his eyes. You are the first person he sees.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你一笔一笔记清楚。有些爱，就落在一张写得明明白白的账上。

ENGLISH: Tell everyone in the inn what happened on the road
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 留下来守伤者一夜

ENGLISH: By evening half the courtyard knows the story. The priest will not be pleased. The wounded man will not be alone again.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 夜里他发起烧来。你用湿布替他擦额头，直到天快亮时他终于睡稳了。

ENGLISH: Ask the innkeeper to keep the coins safe until he returns
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问撒玛利亚人打算什么时候回来

SPEAKER: innkeeper
ENGLISH: The innkeeper wraps them carefully. “He said he would come back,” he mutters. “Most people do not.” He is still holding the coins when you leave.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「我不知道，」他说，「但我会回来。」你知道他说的是真的。

ENGLISH: The road, the inn, the dust — all of it folds back into the scroll. You are sitting in the village again.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 路、客店、尘土，全都折回书卷里。你又坐回了村外。

SPEAKER: jesus
ENGLISH: Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你想，这三个人哪一个是落在强盗手中的邻舍呢？」

SPEAKER: lawyer
ENGLISH: He that shewed mercy on him.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「是怜悯他的。」

SPEAKER: jesus
ENGLISH: Go, and do thou likewise.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「你去照样行吧。」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: He never actually answers “who is my neighbour?” He replaces it with a better question: whose neighbour will you be?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「谁是我的邻舍」这个问题，他其实一直没有回答。他换了一个更好的问题：你愿意成为谁的邻舍？

ENGLISH: Answer with the lawyer: the one who showed mercy
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 把这句话记在自己的书卷上

ENGLISH: Jesus nods. You have understood the parable — which is the easy half.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你把这句话写下来。后来你会一次又一次翻回这一页。

ENGLISH: Answer: the priest, because he knew the Law
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问耶稣：如果我做不到呢

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Corin winces. Jesus gently repeats the story, more slowly this time. Being corrected by kindness is its own kind of mercy.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他看着你，语气里没有责备，只有邀请：「所以你缺的不是意志力，是身边那个具体的人。」

ENGLISH: Stay silent and let the question sit with you
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 回头看一眼那个撒玛利亚人

ENGLISH: You say nothing. But you notice that you can still feel the weight of the man on the donkey. That is a beginning.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他已经上路了，驴背上的位置空着——因为那个人还躺在客店里。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: The lawyer wanted a boundary. Jesus gave him a mirror.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这个比喻里最危险的，不是强盗，而是那条允许你从旁边绕过去的路。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: The neighbour in this story is not a category of person who deserves your help. It is a person you decide to become.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 耶稣没有叫我们做英雄，他叫我们做邻舍。

ENGLISH: The scroll turns. The smell of the road lingers on your clothes.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 书卷翻页了，可那条耶利哥路还在你脚下。

ENGLISH: Peace, Be Still
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 住了吧，静了吧

ENGLISH: The Storm on the Lake
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 湖上的风浪

ENGLISH: A boat, a sudden squall, and a Teacher asleep on a cushion in the stern.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 船在进水，耶稣却在船尾睡着了。

ENGLISH: c. AD 30, evening on the Sea of Galilee — a lake sunk in a bowl of hills, where cold air pours down the slopes and can lift the water into walls within minutes.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 约公元 30 年，傍晚的加利利海。湖被群山围在中间，冷风顺着山坡灌下来，几分钟就能把水面堆成墙。

ENGLISH: Jesus has been teaching from a boat all day. Several of his followers are professional fishermen who have worked this lake their whole lives. He has just said, “Let us pass over unto the other side.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 耶稣在船上讲了一整天。他的门徒里有几个是职业渔夫，在这片湖上讨了半辈子生活。他刚刚说：「我们渡到那边去吧。」

ENGLISH: You are in the boat. When the squall hits, the question stops being about the weather and becomes about the man asleep on the cushion in the stern.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你也在船上。风浪一起来，问题就不再是天气，而是船尾那个枕着枕头睡着的人到底是谁。

ENGLISH: The Sea of Galilee sits in a basin; cold air funnels down from the hills and turns a calm evening into a dangerous squall in minutes. Several of the disciples were experienced fishermen — and they were terrified.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 门徒里好几个是职业渔夫，见过加利利海的风暴。让他们害怕的不是一般的浪，而是那种一下子就把船灌满的狂风。

ENGLISH: Peace is not the absence of the storm. It is who is in the boat.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他没有应许门徒一生都不遇见风浪。他只是选择和门徒一起上了船。

ENGLISH: Jesus asked “why are you so fearful?” while they were still in danger. Faith is not pretending the waves are small; it is knowing the One who made them is aboard.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 风浪来的时候，他就在船尾——他不是不在，只是睡着了。这两件事不一样，可人在凌晨三点很难分得清。

ENGLISH: What storm are you carrying right now — and where do you keep looking?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 此刻你的「船」里正在灌进什么？你最需要听见哪一句？

ENGLISH: The waves — I need to stop staring at them
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「住了吧！静了吧！」——我需要平安

ENGLISH: The disciples were experienced fishermen. Their fear was reasonable. Faith is not the denial of facts; it is a larger fact. Mark 4:38
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他斥责的是风，不是门徒。你的害怕不是他要对付的敌人。马可福音 4:39

ENGLISH: The next small thing I can actually do
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「为什么胆怯？」——我需要勇气

ENGLISH: There is no shame in holding the tiller and bailing while you pray. Psalm 107:29–30
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他先平静了海，然后才问这句话。恩典常常先走一步。马可福音 4:40

ENGLISH: Other people in the boat with me
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「我们渡到那边去吧」——我需要继续往前走

ENGLISH: They were all in it together. Who is in your boat, and how are they doing? Mark 4:36
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这趟船本来就是他提出来的。风浪没有让他的计划落空。马可福音 4:35

ENGLISH: The scroll smells of fish and wet rope. It is evening on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, and a crowd has only just gone home.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 傍晚，加利利海边。你刚听完一整天用比喻讲的道，人群还散在岸上。

SPEAKER: jesus
ENGLISH: Let us pass over unto the other side.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「我们渡到那边去吧。」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: He has been teaching all day. Watch how tired He is. That matters in a few minutes.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 柯林帮着把最后一篮东西搬上船，低声说：「记住这句话。风浪是在他们顺服之后才来的，不是之前。」

ENGLISH: The disciples begin loading a boat. There are other little ships going with them.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 船离了岸。风很轻，水面像锡一样亮。

ENGLISH: Help haul the boat into the water
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 坐到耶稣旁边

ENGLISH: Cold water up to your knees, rope burning your palms. You are useful, and you are soaked.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他在船尾坐下，靠着枕头，几乎立刻就睡着了。

ENGLISH: Check the sky over the hills before boarding
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 帮门徒把帆升起来

ENGLISH: The western sky is clear. But there is a line of dark along the northern ridge that you do not like. Nobody else seems to have noticed.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 绳子磨着你的手心。彼得朝你点点头——这是他再熟悉不过的水面。

ENGLISH: Ask the disciples what kind of man this is
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问柯林，今天讲的比喻是什么意思

SPEAKER: peter
ENGLISH: Peter shrugs. “A good teacher. More than that, I think. We are still finding out.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「撒种的人，」他说，「种子落在四种土里。今晚你会亲眼看见其中一种。」

ENGLISH: The oars settle into a rhythm. The shore slides away. Jesus goes to the stern, lies down on a cushion, and falls asleep almost instantly.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 天色说变就变。加利利海四周的山把风兜下来，像漏斗一样倒进湖里。

SPEAKER: disciple
ENGLISH: He was teaching until sunset. He did not even eat.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「夫子！我们丧命啦！」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Exhaustion is not a lack of faith. He is fully human — which is the very thing this boat is about to forget.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 浪打进来，船里已经积了水。柯林抓着船舷，指节发白。

ENGLISH: Then the wind hits.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这些人是靠海吃饭的渔夫。让他们怕的，不是普通的浪。

ENGLISH: It comes down off the hills like something thrown. The sail cracks. Water comes over the gunwale in a solid sheet.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 而耶稣在船尾，枕着枕头，睡着。

ENGLISH: Grab the tiller and hold the bow into the waves
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 去把耶稣叫醒

ENGLISH: The wood fights you. You fight back. It is the only thing you can do, so you do it.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你爬过湿滑的甲板。他在那儿，呼吸很匀，像躺在岸上一样。

ENGLISH: Start bailing with whatever you can find
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 抓住绳子，把船稳住

ENGLISH: You pass a bucket hand to hand. Someone is praying. Someone else is shouting. Both make sense right now.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 绳子的另一头连着帆。你的手臂发酸，船头总算回过来一点。

ENGLISH: Look toward the stern, where Jesus is
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 先舀水，别的以后再说

ENGLISH: He is still asleep, head on the cushion, while the boat comes apart around Him. You cannot decide if that is terrifying or the calmest thing you have ever seen.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你拿木桶拼命往外舀。水涨得比舀得快，可你没有停。

SPEAKER: peter
ENGLISH: Master! Master, we perish!
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「夫子，我们丧命，你不顾吗？」

ENGLISH: The waves beat into the boat so that it is already filling. The other little ships are vanishing in the spray.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 浪一个接一个翻过船舷。世界只剩下水声、木头的呻吟，还有自己的心跳。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Hold the tiller. Three waves are coming — keep her steady through all three. Breathe between them.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 柯林朝你喊：「别看浪——看掌舵的那只手！」

ENGLISH: Corin puts a hand on your shoulder. “Do the next thing in front of you. That is how trust actually looks in a storm.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你伸手抓住舵柄。风把整条船往一边推。

ENGLISH: The boat is filling. The sail is torn. And in the stern, on a cushion, Jesus is still asleep.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 船一直在进水，帆已经被撕开。船尾上，枕着枕头，耶稣仍旧睡着。

SPEAKER: disciple
ENGLISH: Master, carest thou not that we perish?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「夫子！我们丧命啦！你不顾吗？」

ENGLISH: They shake Him awake. He opens His eyes, looks at the sky, the water, the panic — and stands up.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他们把他摇醒。他睁开眼，看了看天，看了看水，看了看这些慌了的人——然后站起来。

ENGLISH: Wake Him calmly, believing He already cares
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 心里默祷一句最简短的话

ENGLISH: You put a hand on His shoulder without shouting. He looks at you for a moment, and something in His face steadies you before He has said a word.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你想不起一句完整的祷文，只挤出四个字：「主啊，救我！」后来你才知道，这就够了。

ENGLISH: Wake Him in a panic, like everyone else
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 抓住身边最近那个门徒的手

ENGLISH: You shout with the rest. He does not seem offended. Apparently an honest panic is acceptable to Him.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他的手跟你一样凉。你们两个人一起站稳了。恐惧说出口，不会加倍，只会减半。

ENGLISH: Keep bailing until your hands give out
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 什么也不说，只是看着他

ENGLISH: When you finally look up, He is already standing. You did not need to earn His attention. But you could not stop yourself trying.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 风声太大，说什么都会被吹散。可你看得见他的背影。

SPEAKER: jesus
ENGLISH: Peace, be still.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「住了吧！静了吧！」

ENGLISH: The wind does not fade. It stops. The water flattens as though someone has laid a hand on it.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 风不是慢慢小下去的，是一下子就停了。水面平得像有人用手按了一下。

ENGLISH: The silence is so complete you can hear the rope creaking and your own breath.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 静得这样彻底，你能听见绳子吱呀作响，还有自己的呼吸。

SPEAKER: jesus
ENGLISH: Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「为什么胆怯？你们还没有信心吗？」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: He is not asking because He needs the answer. He is asking because you do.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他问这句话，不是因为他需要答案，是因为你需要。

ENGLISH: Whisper: “Lord, I believe; help my unbelief”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 轻声说：「主啊，我信，但我信不足」

ENGLISH: A prayer borrowed from another desperate father, years later. It is still the most honest sentence a person can pray.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这句祷告是借来的，出自多年后另一个绝望的父亲。可它仍是一个人能说出的最诚实的话。

ENGLISH: Ask the question out loud: “Who is this?”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 把心里的话喊出来：「这人到底是谁？」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Mark says they feared exceedingly and said one to another, “What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?” That is the right question.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 马可记载，他们就大大地惧怕，彼此说：「这到底是谁？连风和海也听从他了！」——这就是对的答案。

ENGLISH: Sit in the silence and say nothing at all
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 坐在这一片安静里，什么也不说

ENGLISH: You sit on the wet boards. Someone starts bailing again out of habit, then stops. The lake is glass.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你坐在湿漉漉的甲板上。有人习惯性又舀了一桶水，然后停住。湖面平得像玻璃。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: He did not promise the disciples that they would never meet a storm. He got into the boat with them.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他没有应许门徒一生不遇风浪。他选择跟他们一起上船。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: And when the storm came, He was in the stern — asleep, not absent. There is a difference, though it is hard to remember at 3 a.m.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 风浪来的时候，他就在船尾——他不是不在，只是睡着了。这两件事不一样，可人在凌晨三点很难分得清。

ENGLISH: The far shore is close now. The scroll turns.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 对岸已经近了。书卷翻页。

ENGLISH: The Far Country
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 远方

ENGLISH: The Prodigal Son
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 浪子回头

ENGLISH: A son asks for his inheritance early. His father gives it — and then waits by the road.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 两个儿子，一个父亲。一个离家，一个留下；父亲却为两个人都跑了出去。

ENGLISH: c. AD 30, in Galilee. Jesus is answering religious leaders who complain that he welcomes the wrong people, and he tells three stories in a row about something lost: a sheep, a coin, a son.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 约公元 30 年，加利利。耶稣正在回答宗教领袖的抱怨——他们怪他接待不该接待的人。他一连讲了三个「失而复得」的故事：一只羊、一块钱、一个儿子。

ENGLISH: A father and two sons. The younger asks for his inheritance now — in that culture, the same as saying “I wish you were dead”. The elder stays, works, and keeps every rule.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一位父亲，两个儿子。小儿子现在就要求分家产——在那时的文化里，等于说「我巴不得你死了」。大儿子留下了，干活，规矩一条没犯。

ENGLISH: This story is not mainly about the son who leaves. Watch the father: what he does once the money is gone is the part that would have shocked Jesus’ first listeners.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这个故事真正的主角不是出走的儿子，而是父亲。钱花光以后他做了什么，才是当年听众最受不了的地方。

ENGLISH: This is the third of three “lost” parables in Luke 15 — the lost sheep, the lost coin, and the lost son. It is told because the religious crowd was grumbling that Jesus welcomed sinners.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这是路加福音 15 章三个「失而复得」的故事中的第三个：丢了羊、丢了钱、丢了儿子。耶稣讲这些，是因为宗教人士抱怨他接待罪人。

ENGLISH: Grace is the father running before the apology is finished.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 恩典就是：道歉的话还没说完，父亲已经跑过去抱住了他。

ENGLISH: The father absorbs the cost, restores the ring, and throws a feast — while still going out to plead with the son who never left. He is prodigal, extravagant, with mercy for both.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 父亲为两个儿子都付上了代价：袍子、戒指、鞋、肥牛犊，然后还要走出门去劝那个从没离开过的儿子。对这两个儿子，他都是这样不计代价地爱。

ENGLISH: Which brother are you today — and what would coming home look like?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 今天的你，更像哪一个儿子？对你来说，「回家」会是什么样子？

ENGLISH: The younger: I need to stop rehearsing and start walking
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 小儿子：别再把台词背下去了，该往回走了

ENGLISH: Repentance in Luke 15 is a journey, not a mood. “He arose and came to his father.” Luke 15:20
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 悔改不是在心里难过一阵就够了，而是要真的站起来，转过身，往家走。「于是起来，往他父亲那里去。」路加福音 15:20

ENGLISH: The elder: I have stayed, but my heart is far away
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大儿子：我人留下了，心却离得很远

ENGLISH: The father went out to him too. Obedience without love is its own kind of far country. Luke 15:28–31
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 父亲也为大儿子走了出去。人还留在家里，心一样可以走得很远——顺服里没有爱，人也一样会走丢。路加福音 15:28–31

ENGLISH: The bystander: I want to know how to welcome someone
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 旁观者：我想学会怎么接纳一个人

ENGLISH: Then leave the seat empty and the door open. That is how the parable invites us to finish it. Luke 15:32
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 那就把座位留着，把门开着。耶稣讲这个故事，就是想让我们站在这个位置上。路加福音 15:32

ENGLISH: The scroll opens on a warm courtyard: a large house, olive trees, servants moving between the storehouses. Two sons. One father.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 书卷展开在一座温暖的院子里：大宅、橄榄树、仆人在仓库之间来来去去。两个儿子，一位父亲。

SPEAKER: younger
ENGLISH: Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「父亲，请你把我应得的家业分给我。」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: In that culture, this is not a request for an allowance. It is “I wish you were dead, and I want my share now.” The inheritance would normally come at the funeral.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 在那个年代，这句话不是要零花钱，而是「我巴不得你死了，现在就分给我」。产业本来要等到父亲去世才分。

ENGLISH: The father says nothing for a long moment. Then he divides his living between them.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 父亲沉默了很久。然后，他把产业分给了他们。

ENGLISH: Try to talk the younger son out of it
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 试着劝小儿子回心转意

ENGLISH: He will not even look at you. Somebody has promised him a better story somewhere else, and he can already hear its music.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他连看都没看你。有人已经给他描绘过一个更自在的地方，他连那边的音乐都听见了。

ENGLISH: Ask the father why he agrees to give it
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问父亲为什么答应他

SPEAKER: father
ENGLISH: “Because love that holds on by force is not love,” he says. “I would rather be wounded and keep my son than keep my property and lose him.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「靠扣住家产把人留住，留住的不是爱，只是人，」他说，「我宁可自己受伤，也不要这样。」

ENGLISH: Stand with the servants, who have gone quiet
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 和沉默下来的仆人们站在一起

ENGLISH: They know that a divided estate means some of them will be let go. Nobody in this story is untouched by the son’s choice.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他们清楚，家一分，有些帮工就得走。这个儿子的决定，牵着每一个人的生计。

ENGLISH: Not many days later, the younger son gathers everything, takes a journey into a far country — and spends it all.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 过了不多几日，小儿子把所有的都收拾起来，往远方去了——就在那里散尽了。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Luke uses one devastating phrase: “wasted his substance with riotous living.” No details. We are not invited to enjoy the sin.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 路加用了一句很重的话：「任意放荡，浪费资财。」没有细节。那些罪，没什么好细看的。

ENGLISH: Back home, the father is often on the road, looking toward the horizon.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 而在家里，父亲常常走到路口，望着天边。

SPEAKER: servant
ENGLISH: He goes out there every evening. Every single evening.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「他每天傍晚都出去。每一天。」

ENGLISH: Ask how long the father intends to keep waiting
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问父亲打算等到什么时候

SPEAKER: servant
ENGLISH: The servant shrugs. “Until he comes back, I suppose.” It has been more than a year.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 仆人耸耸肩：「大概是等到他回来吧。」已经一年多了。

ENGLISH: Go out to the road and wait with him
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 到路上陪他一起等

ENGLISH: You stand beside him in the dust until the light fails. He does not say much. He does not need you to.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你在尘土里站到他旁边，直到天光褪尽。他没说多少话，也不需要你说。

ENGLISH: Follow the younger son into the far country
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 跟着小儿子去远方

ENGLISH: You find a city that is bright at night and expensive in the morning. His friends are already gone when the money runs out.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你找到一座城：夜里灯火通明，白天什么都贵。钱花光以后，他的朋友一个都不见了。

ENGLISH: A mighty famine rises in that land. The son, who once threw money from a table, now hires himself out to a citizen — to feed pigs.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 那地方遇上大饥荒。从前把钱往外撒的儿子，如今去投靠本地一个人——替他放猪。

ENGLISH: He is so hungry that the pods the pigs eat look good to him. And no one gives him anything.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他饿到觉得猪吃的豆荚都是好东西。可没有人给他。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: For a Jewish listener, pigs are the bottom. Luke could not have made the fall steeper.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 对当时的犹太听众来说，猪圈已经是最低的地方了——再往下，就没有了。

SPEAKER: younger
ENGLISH: He came to himself.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「他醒悟过来。」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Four words. The turning point of the whole parable. He does not get rescued first — he comes to himself.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 四个字。整个比喻在这里拐了个弯。他不是先被救出来——他是先醒过来。

ENGLISH: Remind him that his father’s hired servants have bread
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 提醒他：父亲家里连雇工都有饼吃

SPEAKER: younger
ENGLISH: The thought lands like a physical blow. “Bread,” he says. “Even the servants.” He has not thought of home in months.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这句话像打了他一拳。「连雇工，」他喃喃地说，「都有饼吃。」他已经好几个月没想起家了。

ENGLISH: Sit in the mud with him until he can speak
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 陪他坐在泥里，等他自己开口

ENGLISH: You say nothing. After a long time he says, “I have to go back.” You nod. He needs to hear himself say it.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你什么也没说。过了很久，他说：「我得回去。」你点点头——他需要听见自己说出口。

ENGLISH: Help him rehearse the words: “Father, I have sinned”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 陪他把「父亲，我得罪了」练一遍

ENGLISH: He practises it out loud, twice, and then a third time. He is preparing to return as a servant, not a son.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他大声练了两遍，又练了第三遍。他想好了：回去做雇工，不做儿子。

SPEAKER: younger
ENGLISH: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee, and am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「我要起来，到我父亲那里去，向他说：父亲！我得罪了天，又得罪了你；从今以后，我不配称为你的儿子，把我当作一个雇工吧！」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Repentance in this story is not a feeling of regret. It is a direction. He stands up and starts walking — hundreds of miles, in the same sandals he wore into the pigsty.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这个故事里，悔改不是心里懊悔一下，而是一个方向。他站起来开始走——几百里路，穿的还是走进猪圈时那双鞋。

ENGLISH: The road is long. He gets quieter the closer he gets to home.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 路很长。离家越近，他越说不出话。

ENGLISH: Walk with him as far as the last ridge
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 陪他走到最后一道山脊

ENGLISH: At the top he stops, and you see the roof of the house below. He is crying. You leave him there — the last part is his.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 到了山脊上他停住了。你看见山下那座房子的屋顶。他在哭。你先走开几步——最后这一程，得他自己走。

ENGLISH: Run ahead and warn the household
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 先跑回家去报信

ENGLISH: You burst into the courtyard shouting. The father is already running past you before you finish the sentence.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你冲进院子大喊。话还没说完，父亲已经从你身边跑了出去。

ENGLISH: Ask Corin whether the father will take him back
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问柯林，父亲会不会收他

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Corin smiles. “You have read this story before,” he says. “Watch the father’s feet.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 柯林笑了：「你从前读过这个故事吧。留意父亲的脚。」

ENGLISH: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「于是起来，往他父亲那里去。相离还远，他父亲看见他。」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: He saw him a great way off — because he had been looking. Every evening. For years.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 相离还远就看见了——因为他一直在看。每个傍晚，看了好几年。

ENGLISH: The father runs. In that culture, a patriarch does not run; it is undignified. He does not care. He falls on his son’s neck and kisses him.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 父亲跑过去。在那个文化里，一家之主是不跑的，那很失体面。他不在乎。他搂住他的脖子，连连亲他。

SPEAKER: younger
ENGLISH: Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son —
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「父亲！我得罪了天，又得罪了你；从今以后，我不配称为你的儿子——」

SPEAKER: father
ENGLISH: Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet! And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry!
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「快把上好的袍子拿出来给他穿，把戒指戴在他指头上，把鞋穿在他脚上；把那肥牛犊牵来宰了，我们可以吃喝快乐！」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: He never lets his son finish the sentence. The rehearsed speech about becoming a hired servant is cut off by a party.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 儿子的话没说完。那段排练好的、关于做雇工的讲词，被一场筵席打断了。

ENGLISH: Run alongside the father to meet him
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 跟着父亲一起跑出去迎他

SPEAKER: father
ENGLISH: You arrive out of breath in time to see the ring go onto a hand that is still shaking. “My son was dead, and is alive again,” the father keeps saying.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你气喘吁吁赶到，正看见戒指套上一只还在发抖的手。「我这个儿子是死而复活，」父亲一遍一遍地说。

ENGLISH: Weep at the edge of the crowd
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 站在人群边上哭

ENGLISH: You are not family. You are not a servant. You are nobody in this story. And still you cannot stop crying. That is what grace does to bystanders.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你不是家人，也不是仆人。在这个故事里你谁都不是。可你还是止不住眼泪——站在旁边看见恩典的人，都是这样。

ENGLISH: Fetch the best robe yourself
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 亲自去取那件上好的袍子

ENGLISH: The robe is heavy and smells of cedar. You put it over shoulders that are still covered in pig-sty dust. Nobody seems to mind.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 袍子很沉，有香柏木的味道。你把它披在一副还沾着猪圈尘土的肩上。好像没人在意这些。

ENGLISH: Music. Dancing. Lamps in the courtyard. And then the story turns — because the elder son is out in the field.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 音乐、舞蹈、院子里的灯。然后故事拐了个弯——大儿子还在田里。

SPEAKER: elder
ENGLISH: What do these things mean? Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment — and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends! But as soon as this thy son was come, which hath devoured thy living, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf!
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「我服事你这多年，从来没有违背过你的命，你并没有给我一只山羊羔，叫我和朋友一同快乐。」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Notice: “this thy son.” He will not say “my brother.” He is not wrong about the facts. He is wrong about the family.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 留意他说的是「你这个儿子」。他不肯说「我的兄弟」。论事实，他没有说错；可论关系，他离得还很远。

ENGLISH: The father goes out and pleads with him. He leaves the party to stand in the dark with the son who stayed.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 父亲出去劝他。他离开筵席，走进黑地里，去陪那个留下来的儿子。

ENGLISH: Go out and listen to the elder brother
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 出去听大儿子把话说完

ENGLISH: You stand in the field with him. He is not angry at the party, really. He is hurt that nobody noticed he never left.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你和他一起站在田里。他真正气的不是筵席，是没有人注意到——他从来没离开过。

ENGLISH: Tell him he is being unfair
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 直接告诉他这不公平

ENGLISH: You say it plainly. He says something sharp back. Later you will wish you had asked a question instead.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你照直说了。他顶了你一句。后来你会希望当时多问一句，而不是先下判断。

ENGLISH: Ask the father why he goes out to both sons
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问父亲：为什么两个儿子，你都要出去找

SPEAKER: father
ENGLISH: “Because both of them are lost,” he says. “One was lost far away. One is lost three feet from my table.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「因为两个都迷了路，」他说，「一个迷在远方，一个迷在离我饭桌三步远的地方。」

SPEAKER: father
ENGLISH: Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine. It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「儿啊，你常和我同在，我一切所有的都是你的；只是你这个兄弟是死而复活、失而又得的，所以我们理当欢喜快乐。」

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: The parable ends there. Jesus never tells us whether the elder brother came inside. That silence is deliberate — because the people He was speaking to were the elder brothers, and the ending was up to them.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 比喻就停在这里。耶稣没有说大儿子最后有没有进屋。这份沉默是故意的——因为当年听他讲道的人，正是那些大儿子。结局得他们自己写。

ENGLISH: You look at the lit doorway. Then you look at the dark field.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你看了看那扇亮着灯的门，又看了看黑下来的田。

ENGLISH: Stand with the elder brother in the dark, and wait
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 站在黑地里，陪大儿子一起等

ENGLISH: You do not push. You just stay. Sometimes that is the only invitation a person can accept.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你没有催促他，也没有急着劝他，只是安静地留在他身边。因为有时候，一个人最需要的，不是有人告诉他该怎么走出来，而是有人愿意陪着他，等他慢慢走出来。

ENGLISH: Remind him gently that he is already inside the family
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 温和地提醒他：他早就在这个家里

ENGLISH: “All that I have is thine,” you repeat. He looks at the house for a long time. It is the truest thing anyone has said to him all day.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「我一切所有的都是你的，」你把这句话重复了一遍。他望着那幢房子，望了很久。这是他一天里听到的最真实的一句话。

ENGLISH: Go back to the feast and keep his seat empty
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 回到筵席，把他的座位留着

ENGLISH: You set an extra place at the table, just in case. The music goes on. The door stays open.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你多摆了一副餐具，以防万一。音乐没有停，门也一直开着。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Two sons. One runs away, one stays and resents it. The father runs after both.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 两个儿子。一个出走，一个留下却满心怨气。父亲为两个人都跑了出去。

SPEAKER: elias
ENGLISH: Most of us have been the younger son at some point. Quite a lot of us have been the elder one for years and never noticed.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 我们多半在某一段时间里是小儿子；也有不少人做了很多年的大儿子，自己却没察觉。

ENGLISH: The scroll turns, but the music from the courtyard follows you down the road.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 书卷翻页，院子里的音乐却一路跟着你。

ENGLISH: For Such a Time
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 为现今的机会

ENGLISH: Queen Esther
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 以斯帖王后

ENGLISH: A decree of destruction. A queen who has not been summoned. One line in the law that could cost her everything.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这卷书一次也没有提到神，却处处都是祂安排的时间。

ENGLISH: c. 480 BC, in Susa, the winter capital of Persia — the largest empire in the world at the time. The queen, Esther, is Jewish, and almost nobody in the palace knows it.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 约公元前 480 年，波斯帝国的冬都书珊城。以斯帖是王后，也是犹太人——宫里几乎没有人知道这件事。

ENGLISH: Haman, the king’s favourite, was publicly refused a bow by Mordecai — a Jew, and Esther’s older cousin, who raised her. So Haman has drawn up a decree: on one day, every Jew in the empire may be killed. The king has signed it.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 王的宠臣哈曼，因为犹太人末底改不肯向他下拜，怀恨在心。末底改是以斯帖的堂兄，也是把她养大的人。哈曼拟了一道诏书：某一天，全国各省的犹太人都可以任人宰杀。王已经盖了印。

ENGLISH: Esther is the only person close enough to the king to intervene, and he has not called for her in thirty days. Walking into the throne room uninvited is a death sentence unless he holds out his golden sceptre.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 能接近王的只有以斯帖，可王已经三十天没有召见她。没有召见就闯进宝座殿，是死罪——除非王向她伸出金杖。

ENGLISH: Approaching the Persian king unsummoned carried the death penalty unless he extended the golden sceptre. Esther had not been called for thirty days. The book of Esther is unusual — God is never named in it — yet His providence is everywhere in the timing.

ENGLISH: I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.

ENGLISH: It is the same answer Abraham gave. Some sentences are handed down like a family trade.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 这也是亚伯拉罕当年的回答。有些话，就这么一代一代传下来了。

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问祂的名字是什么

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 答案慢慢浮出来：「我是我所是」（出埃及记 3:14）。这不是一个能攥在手里的名号，而是一位一直都在的神。

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 什么也不说，只是跪着

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 沉默也是一种回答。火焰等着你。

SPEAKER: moses

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 我算什么，竟能去见法老呢？

ENGLISH: Notice: God does not answer “you are qualified.” He answers “I will be with you.”

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他接过去，掂了掂分量。一根杖算不了什么——可上路的人手里总得有点什么。

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 请他记住这座山

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 「我会的，」他说，「特别是在那些我宁愿忘掉的日子里。」

ENGLISH: The call did not make Moses fearless. It made him accompanied. That is the whole difference.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 呼召并没有让摩西不再惧怕，而是让他不再孤单。区别就在这里。

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你回头看了一眼。荆棘仍在燃烧——安静、耐心，完全没有观众。

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 书卷翻页。埃及还很远。

ENGLISH: The Gleaning Field
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 拾穗的麦田

ENGLISH: Ruth and Naomi
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 路得与拿俄米

ENGLISH: Two widows walk home with nothing. One of them refuses to leave the other.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 两个寡妇空着手走回家。其中一个怎么也不肯离开另一个。

ENGLISH: c. 1100 BC, in Bethlehem at the start of the barley harvest. A famine has just broken; the fields are full and the town is full of talk.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 约公元前 1100 年，伯利恒，大麦刚开镰。饥荒刚过去，田里满是庄稼，城里满是闲话。

ENGLISH: Naomi came back from Moab with nothing — no husband, no sons, and a foreign daughter-in-law, Ruth, who refused to stay behind. Ruth is a Moabite, and Moabites are not welcome here.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 拿俄米从摩押回来时一无所有：丈夫没了，两个儿子也没了，只剩下一个外族媳妇路得，怎么劝都不肯走。路得是摩押人，而摩押人在伯利恒不受欢迎。

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 两个寡妇没有收入，也没有男人可以依靠。律法允许穷人在收割的人后面捡拾掉落的麦穗——路得就是去那里找吃的，田主第一次看见她，也是在那里。

ENGLISH: Ruth was a Moabite — an outsider with no status in Bethlehem. Gleaning was the ancient safety net: the poor could follow the reapers and pick up what was dropped. Boaz's generosity turns a survival mechanism into a love story.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 路得是摩押人——在伯利恒抬不起头的外乡人。拾穗是古时给穷人的活路：跟在收割的人后面，捡掉在地上的麦穗。波阿斯多留的那几把麦穗，成了这段爱情的开头。

ENGLISH: Loyalty is love that has kept walking after the feeling fades.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 忠诚不是一直有感觉，而是感觉淡了以后，还继续走下去。

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 路得那段著名的话，其实不是情话，而是一个儿媳对一位年老伤心的婆婆许下的承诺。神看重这份微小又固执的善良，把它编进了弥赛亚的家谱。

ENGLISH: Who is the person you would “go with” even when it costs you?
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 谁是你愿意「一同前往」的人，即使要付代价？

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 年迈的父母或祖父母

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 路得选择的，是那个最无法回报她的人。路得记 1:16–17

ENGLISH: A friend who is struggling
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一位正在挣扎的朋友

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 陪伴是最难得的礼物，因为它没法隔空送过去。路得记 1:16

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 我还不确定有没有这样的人

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 那就从小事开始：这一次在场，下一次也在场。忠诚就是这么一天一天攒出来的。路得记 1:16

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 问柯林，路得为何选择吃苦

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你还不知道，这个祷告会怎样一字不差地应验。

SPEAKER: ruth
ENGLISH: Let me glean, I pray you, after him in whose sight I shall find grace.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 求你容我跟着收割的人，拾取打捆剩下的麦穗。

ENGLISH: This is not charity as a spectacle. It is a law written into the edges of a field — leave something for the person who has nothing. Leviticus 19:9

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 陪她拾一整个下午的麦穗

ENGLISH: Ask the reapers to leave extra behind
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 请收割的人多留一些麦穗

ENGLISH: They shrug, then grin, and suddenly a whole corner of the field is 'accidentally' uncut.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他们耸耸肩，咧嘴一笑——忽然间，整块田角都「不小心」没割到。

ENGLISH: Sit with Naomi at the edge of the field
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 陪拿俄米坐在田边

ENGLISH: She watches Ruth work and says only: “She has not stopped. Not once.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 她看着路得干活，只说了一句：「她一直没停。一次都没有。」

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 波阿斯没有讲一篇关于仁慈的大道理，只是吩咐拿镰刀的人一句话。真正的仁慈，就是这样一点一点落到实处的。

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 留意这条线：一个外邦寡妇，一块田，几把故意落下的麦穗。没有人称它为神迹，可这就是大卫的家谱——后来也是耶稣的家谱。

ENGLISH: Thank Boaz on Ruth’s behalf
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 替路得向波阿斯道谢

ENGLISH: He waves it away. “She did the hard part,” he says. “I only told my men to look the other way.”
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 他摆摆手：「难的那部分是她自己做的。我只是叫工人别看得那么紧。」

ENGLISH: Tell Naomi what happened in the field
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 把田里发生的事告诉拿俄米

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 你什么也没说。路得始终不知道你的名字。那也是一种爱。

ENGLISH: Ruth did not save Israel. She simply refused to leave one person. Great stories are usually built out of small refusals.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 路得没有拯救以色列，她只是不肯离开一个人。许多伟大的故事，就是从一个很小的「不肯」开始的。

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 太阳落在大麦田上。拿俄米抱着篮子回家；路得牵着拿俄米的手。

ENGLISH: The scroll turns, smelling faintly of cut grain.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 书卷翻页，带着淡淡的麦香。

ENGLISH: The Great Fish
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 大鱼腹中

ENGLISH: Jonah and Nineveh
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 约拿与尼尼微

ENGLISH: A prophet runs the wrong way, a storm follows him, and mercy waits at the bottom of the sea.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 一位先知往反方向跑，风暴追着他，而怜悯在海底等着他。

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 约公元前 780 年。尼尼微是亚述的京城，当时最令人生畏的帝国——大到圣经说走遍全城要三天。

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 神叫先知约拿到尼尼微去，向那座城宣告审判，好让他们回转。约拿却买了船票，往相反方向的他施去。

CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 海上起了风暴。水手们为了活命什么都肯做，而这场风暴的起因，正睡在船舱里——一个想逃掉唯一躲不掉的那件事的先知。

ENGLISH: Jonah is the reluctant prophet: he runs because he suspects God will be merciful to Nineveh — and he would rather they were judged. The book ends with God asking a question He does not answer, leaving the reader to examine their own reluctance to forgive.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 约拿是不情愿的先知：他逃跑，是因为他猜到神会怜悯尼尼微——而他宁愿他们被审判。这卷书最后，神问了一个问题，却没有给答案，好让读者看看自己心里那份不肯饶恕。

ENGLISH: Mercy is hardest when it is given to people you dislike.
CHINESE (rewrite this column, keep the I: 怜悯落到你讨厌的人身上时，最难接受——可那才是怜悯。
